media.alt: World renowned cardiologist leads workshop at AKU

content.text: He is one of the world's leading interventional cardiologists - a recipient of countless international awards and honours including Recognition Awards from the American Heart Association, the Indian National Institute of Heart Diseases and the Pakistan Society of Cardiology. His breadth of experience spans military assignments, academic positions, hospital appointments, and administrative responsibilities. He is currently an Executive Director of the Interventional Cardiology Research Institute in Maryland, a Director of Interventional Cardiology at Washington Adventist Hospital and a Clinical Professor of Cardiology at the George Washington University School of Medicine in Washington D.C. and also serves on the editorial boards of several medical journals.

On February 27, 1999, the Aga Khan University (AKU) hosted a full day cardiology workshop led by the eminent Dr Fayyaz A. Shawl. Held at the AKU Auditorium, the workshop titled, "Update on interventional Cardiology," was part of AKU's Continuing Medical Education programme for physicians, residents and interns. Some hundred eminent cardiologists and cardiac surgeons from the country's medical community were invited to participate in this valuable learning experience and to share the opportunity to upgrade their knowledge and skills in interventional cardiology.

During the workshop, Dr Shawl performed several interventional procedures on selected patients brought to AKU from all over Pakistan. Patients with unique cardiac problems requiring treatment currently not available in the country were able to benefit from Dr Shawl's advanced expertise. Meanwhile, participants viewed the procedures transmitted live from Aga Khan University Hospital's Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory to the AKU Auditorium.

Dr Shawl had been invited by AKU on the initiative of Mr Mumtaz A. Rahim of Brinks Securities with support from other corporate sponsors such as Abbott Laboratories, Toshiba as well as Johnson and Johnson. Arrangements were also made for Dr Shawl to deliver a lecture at the National Institute for Cardiovascular Diseases while he was a guest of AKU.
